correctness.rationale: The defining bracket descends from a log-canonical Poisson bracket and is valid over every field. A degree-two square argument restricts first jets to monomial matrices outside characteristic two; Poisson signs force diagonal matrices. In characteristic two direct expansion shows every invertible linear substitution is Poisson. The kernel has a central degree filtration [K_r,K_s] subset K_(r+s-1); the binary GL3 subgroup generated by commutators proves nonsolvability at m>=3. At m=2 every admissible first jet has q^2 quadratic lifts. The standalone finite-enumeration program verifies the stated small-field formulas; it does not replace the uniform proof.

value.rationale: The claim classifies a canonical global automorphism-group quotient for an infinite family of nilpotent Poisson algebras over arbitrary fields, proves its kernel nilpotent, and gives a sharp transition from universally solvable to nonsolvable full symmetry groups. This is not a mere finite data point or parity check: a nontrivial perfect subgroup appears uniformly for m>=3 in characteristic two and is excluded in all other characteristics. The finite-field jet orders make the structural difference quantitatively exact.
